clue.text: Stubbornness ruined body defending posh group of drivers

indicators.note: to defend something is to stand around it, so the shuffled word wraps the other letters
something ruined is wrecked out of its proper shape, so the word next to it is rearranged

parts.note: the word itself, to be rearranged
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A motoring club's members are being stubborn about protecting a damaged car body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'body' looks like the car's bodywork, but it is just the letters to shuffle; the inserted pair lands just after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: Obduracy is a noun for hard-hearted refusal to change one's mind, a direct synonym of stubbornness.

clue.text: Contemplate banning outsiders being legitimate

indicators.note: excluding the outsiders means the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: to consider is to contemplate

explanation.surface: Someone ponders whether excluding foreigners is lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: Onside, as in football, means not offside, so within the rules and legitimate.

clue.text: Bird beginning to swoop in part for fish

parts.note: a dove is a bird

indicators.note: in places this letter inside the next word

parts.note: a part played by an actor

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A bird starts to dive, playing its part in catching fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover sole is a flatfish prized for eating, an example of a fish.

clue.text: Wash some workwear in sequence

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is used

parts.note: letters running across the words

explanation.surface: Launder work clothes one batch after another.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash with clean water, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Arab in African country supported by European in absurd behaviour

indicators.note: in a down clue what supports comes underneath, so this letter goes after
in places this abbreviation inside the next word

parts.note: Chad, a country in central Africa
AR is a standard abbreviation for Arab or Arabic
E is an abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: An Arab visitor in Africa, backed by a European, behaves ridiculously.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence or farcical show, behaviour that is plainly ridiculous.

clue.text: Trashy equipment supplied by school

indicators.note: one thing supplied by another has the second thing added after it, so the pieces run in order

parts.note: kit is gear or equipment
standard abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: Cheap, nasty equipment provided by a school to its pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch describes art or objects in tasteless, cheap, sentimental style, which is what trashy means here.

clue.text: Drug that is probed by British university academic and knight

indicators.note: something probed has another thing pushed into it, so the letters go inside

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is
B is an abbreviation for British
U is an abbreviation for university
short for professor
N is chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A medicine is investigated by a British professor who happens to be knighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' stands for 'that is', the Latin id est; the knight is N from chess notation, since K is taken by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a common anti-inflammatory painkiller, an example of a drug.

clue.text: Bend also found in Spain

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it

parts.note: SP is an abbreviation for Spain
too means also

explanation.surface: A bend in the road also turns up in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoop is to bend the body forwards and downwards, a synonym of bend.

clue.text: Senior diplomat with a country house almost close to collapse — source of worry?

indicators.note: almost all of it means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
taken as written
a dacha is a Russian country house

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An ambassador's rural mansion is on the verge of falling down: a real worry.
explanation.walkthrough: HE is His Excellency, the formal address for an ambassador; a dacha is a Russian country house, here losing its last A.
explanation.definitionFit: A headache in the figurative sense is a troublesome problem, something that causes worry.

clue.text: A vehicle kept by retired German in US port

indicators.note: what is kept by something is held inside it, so the first letters go within the others
retiring means going back, so the name is written backwards

parts.note: a typical German man's name
a van is a vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A retired German man in an American port town keeps a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Using a typical first name to stand for a nationality is a crossword habit, and 'retired' turns the name round before it takes in the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Savannah is a city and seaport in the state of Georgia, USA.

clue.text: Sporting contest a timeless group backed in dome

parts.note: a cup competition, like the FA Cup

indicators.note: to back something is to move it backwards, so these letters run in the opposite direction
without time means losing the letter that abbreviates time

parts.note: taken as written
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A sports tournament crowd gathers under a stadium dome.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the standard abbreviation for time, so 'timeless' drops that letter before the group is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupola is a small rounded dome on a roof, so dome is a near synonym.

clue.text: Latest character bringing up low cinematic technique?

parts.note: the last letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to low is to make the sound of cattle

explanation.surface: The newest film character brings in a lowly camera trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the verb for a cow's noise, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A zoom is a camera shot that moves quickly closer to or away from its subject, one film technique.

clue.text: A number for departure?

parts.note: surface reading: a tune played as someone leaves, or a gate or flight number
setter's reading: a number is a song, and departure is death, so a funeral song

explanation.walkthrough: 'Departure' suggests airports and trains, but here it is the final departure; 'number' is a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a slow mournful song or lament sung at a funeral for the dead.

clue.text: A priest, old chap moved when digesting extremes of religiosity in unorthodox books

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something digesting takes food inside itself, so the letters swallow others
letters that are moved are shifted about into a fresh order

parts.note: P is an abbreviation for priest
O for old, plus chap as written

indicators.note: extremes are the outermost ends, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A priest and an old fellow are changed by reading heterodox religious texts.
explanation.walkthrough: O for old is a crossword standard; 'moved' shuffles only the old chap, and the shuffled letters then swallow the two ends of religiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are scriptural writings of doubtful authority excluded from the accepted biblical canon, hence unorthodox books.

clue.text: Item in section of verse cut short

indicators.note: cutting something short trims off its tail, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: a couplet is a pair of rhyming lines in a poem

explanation.surface: A literature student trims a passage of poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item' is the romantic sense, two people going out together, not an object in a list.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is informally a romantic pair, so it means the same as a couple.

clue.text: Blame about to be forgotten in testing period

indicators.note: what is forgotten is left out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: reprobation is strong disapproval or censure
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Criticism is soon forgotten during a trial period at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Probation is a trial period in which a new employee's suitability is assessed.

clue.text: Second rousing cheer enveloping sports body and athlete

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
the Football Association, English football's governing body

explanation.walkthrough: The second and the cheer together wrap round the sports body. Mo Farah is a British distance runner, four-time Olympic champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Mo Farah is a famous long-distance runner, an example of an athlete.

clue.text: Awkward to-do amid bow, say, in part of church

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: bow is the oarsman nearest the front of a boat, an example of a rower

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsily arranged, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the word itself, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An embarrassing fuss breaks out during a bow, perhaps at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow' looks like a bend of the body; in rowing it is the crew member seated nearest the bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood tower is the tower over the crossing of a church, where the rood or cross stands.

clue.text: Preserve trailed by celebrated baseball player in capital

indicators.note: something trailed by another has that second thing following behind it

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it
Yogi Berra, the famous New York Yankees catcher

explanation.surface: A famous ballplayer follows a tinned preserve around a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Canberra is the capital city of Australia.

clue.text: Dubious name associated with individual plant

parts.note: the word itself, to be rearranged
one is a single, individual thing

explanation.surface: A questionable label is attached to a particular plant specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone is a flowering plant of the buttercup family, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Fair English archdeacon

parts.note: E is an abbreviation for English
an archdeacon is addressed as the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' is not a pale complexion here but equitable, and archdeacons are styled the Venerable.
explanation.definitionFit: Even can mean equal or balanced, and so fair, as in an even contest.

clue.text: Report of official banning device to detect change?

parts.note: a censor is an official who bans material

explanation.surface: An official's report bans a gadget for spotting changes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensor is an instrument that detects and responds to a change in its environment, like light or heat.

clue.text: Australia encapsulated by scornful former President

clue.text: Drink obtained by German musician in audition
